hypotheses.justification: The hypothesis is only used for `ht.1 : 0 ≤ t`, in the phase-2 and phase-3 branches. In `rhoC`, the first branch (`t ≤ params.phi`) gives the constant 1/2. Every later branch is reached only when `¬ t ≤ params.phi`, so `params.phi < t`. The lemma `phi_nonneg : 0 ≤ params.phi` (line 662, no arguments) then gives `0 ≤ t`. In the proof, `hφ : ¬ t ≤ params.phi` is in context after `split_ifs`. So `have ht0 : 0 ≤ t := le_trans phi_nonneg (le_of_lt (lt_of_not_ge hφ))` replaces `ht.1` in the phase-2 and phase-3 calls to `rhoC_phase2_nonneg` and `rhoC_phase3_nonneg`. The phase-4 branch already derives `0 ≤ t` from `eta ≤ t` (it never uses `ht`). The last branch is 0. The upper bound `t ≤ T` is never used. So the statement `∀ t, 0 ≤ rhoC t` holds without the hypothesis. `T` is still needed by `rhoC` through `tau` and `eta`, so deleting the binder does not break elaboration.
